Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-14 15:30 PDT

Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Alex Martin (Peregrine CTO), Priya Singh (Eng Mgr), Luis Ortega (SRE)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro: Jordan here, AE on the PLG team, Priya's the SE, she'll cover technical details. Appreciate you taking time, Alex?
[00:08] Alex (Peregrine): Yeah thanks, Jordan. We're excited to hear how Redwood might fit our plan for a PLG flow. We're trying to get to first token as quickly as possible for devs, and then scale to production.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick high-level — Redwood's quickstart is designed for exactly that: we give credits, a tiny SDK sample, and you can be calling the hosted API in minutes. Then customers can opt into Dedicated or Private later.
[00:30] Priya Singh (Peregrine Eng Mgr): When you say "minutes", can you clarify steps? We have dev PDs who will poke at this today if it's easy.
[00:38] Jordan: Sure. Sign up, grab API key, run the quickstart script (node/python), post a prompt — you get streaming within ~30s to first response in a standard PLG case. We'll send a step-by-step doc and free credits.
[00:52] Luis (SRE): What's the limits on the free credits, and is there rate limiting that could affect time-to-first-token? Also curious about cold-start latency on GPU-backed models.
[01:05] Priya: Credits are typically enough for a small pilot — we'll include exact quotas in the email. For rate limits we have default quotas but for the trial we can adjust. Cold starts vary by model: hosted smaller models are sub-200ms per token in many cases, larger open models can be 400-800ms first token depending on size and batching. We also do prefix caching and K-V cache reuse to improve tail latency.
[01:30] Alex: That K-V cash — sorry — K-V cash, I think you meant KV cache? We run a lot of context window workloads so that's important.
[01:36] Priya: Right, KV cache — sorry, auto-transcript will mess that up — we manage KV to avoid re-computing past tokens.
[01:42] Jordan: And just to be clear, for initial PLG we recommend hosted to move fast, then if you need predictable throughput we talk Dedicated pools. Private/VPC is available if you need customer isolation.
[01:55] Alex: What does Dedicated look like from a commit perspective? We have seasonal spikes and don't want to overcommit.
[02:02] Priya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with autoscaling policies and burst options. You can set a baseline commit and enable burst capacity. For pilots we often start with hosted + a small dedicated reservation for predictable latency experiments.
[02:15] Luis: For security, we need SOC 2, SSO integration (SAML), audit logs, and KMS-backed key management. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[02:25] Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments. Hosted has envelope encryption and rotation, and we provide SOC 2 docs. We'll share the security pack. For SSO, we do SAML/SCIM + RBAC.
[02:40] Priya Singh: Is there a way to limit data retention for logs? We're in regulated verticals and need selective retention or deletion policies.
[02:47] Priya: We have log retention controls in the Console; for Private deployments you can set retention to zero and we support audit logs to your SIEM.
[02:55] Alex: Ok good. From a cost perspective, how do you think about latency vs cost? Our product team is split: some want lowest latency always, others want to optimize cost for lower value calls.
[03:05] Priya: We provide levers: batching, caching, model quantization profiles, and routing policies. You can route high-priority requests to Dedicated low-latency pools and lower-priority to cheaper hosted variants. We can show a cost vs latency chart in the demo.
[03:20] Jordan: For the pilot, recommend capturing 3 prompts: low-latency critical path, medium, and batch/async flows. Those will map to quantization and routing configs.
[03:30] Alex: Sounds good. On the engineering side, how invasive is integration? We have a Node backend and a serverless edge layer.
[03:38] Priya: Minimal. Our SDKs (Node/Python) are a few lines. You can also call the REST endpoint directly. We have streaming helpers for serverless. The biggest ops work is if you go Private — then network setup (VPC peering, KMS) and infra coordination.
[03:55] Luis: Private is interesting for us; a question: for on-prem, how does the control plane work? We need air-gapped options.
[04:02] Priya: We provide an optional private control plane that can run in your VPC or on-prem with a connector. For air-gapped, we have an on-prem package; it's heavier but meets the reqs. We'll share the deployment doc.
[04:15] Alex: Excellent. One more practical: do you provide sample benchmarks or a spreadsheet we can drop our payloads into?
[04:22] Jordan: Yes, we'll share a benchmark template. Priya can run a short run with your sample payloads during the follow-up demo.
[04:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Quick technical note on model variants: we maintain curated open models and smaller quantized variants for cost-sensitive paths. For production we recommend validating output quality on a small eval set to avoid regressions when using quantized variants.
[04:47] Priya Singh: That evaluation piece is critical — we need guardrails for quality regressions. Does Redwood support eval hooks or can we run A/B?
[04:55] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize has eval integration and can run A/B/canary rollouts with automatic fallback. We'll demo the rollouts and the alerting tied to prompt sets.
[05:05] Speaker 1: Uh-huh, can you talk about token-level cost visibility?
[05:09] Jordan: Console shows token-level breakdown by route/model with cost and latency. Very helpful to identify hot paths.
[05:15] Alex: Ok, timeline — we'd like to get internal sign-off this month and run a pilot next week if possible. Do you think that's realistic?
[05:22] Priya: For the PLG quickstart, yes — you can be live calling APIs in <24 hours. For a pilot with benchmarks we'll allocate 1-2 weeks for validation.
[05:30] Jordan: We'll send the credits today and the quickstart doc. Priya will run the demo and help set up the benchmark.
[05:36] Luis: One more about networking: if we do hosted, do we need to open any inbound to your infra or is it outbound only?
[05:42] Priya: Outbound only for hosted. For VPC/Private there will be peering or connector setup.
[05:48] Alex: Great. Any known gotchas for Node serverless streaming that we should prepare for?
[05:54] Priya: Just make sure you handle reconnects and backpressure; our SDK includes helpers, but under heavy burst you may want to use smaller streaming chunks. We'll share best-practices doc.
[06:05] Priya Singh: Security follow-up: I'll run the security checklist with Luis and we'll flag anything missing.
[06:11] Jordan: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[06:14] Jordan: Action items: I'll send quickstart + credits; Priya will schedule demo and run benchmark; Luis will share network/KMS specifics.
[06:25] Alex: Sounds good, thanks Jordan/Priya. Looking forward to the demo.
[06:30] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and drop the docs in the thread.
